title: [human][BUG] oscore-fork 0.1.3: two distinct ContextId types break external SenderStateStore impls (E0053)
description: Precise diagnosis from worker1's 4k15 round (Rust ASSIGNED_SF slice): the fork (oscore-fork 0.1.3, commit 1c56f30) now has TWO distinct ContextId types — ~/crates/oscore/src/types.rs:86 (used by the new SenderStateStore trait at types.rs:104, commit 1c56f30) and ~/crates/oscore/src/lib.rs:205 (the original, re-exported by lichen-oscore's grouped pub use oscore::{...}). The trait's method signatures bind to types::ContextId, so every EXTERNAL impl of SenderStateStore using the re-exported lib.rs ContextId fails E0053 — reproduced in lichen-node/src/rpl_stack/tests.rs:84,101 (expected oscore::types::ContextId, found ContextId); lichen-node lib tests cannot compile. Fix direction (Mark decides, oscore boundary): (a) delete the types.rs:86 duplicate and have types.rs use the canonical lib.rs ContextId, or (b) have lichen-oscore re-export oscore::types::ContextId and migrate internals. Either rewrites trait signatures inside the oscore boundary — filed per the oscore human-only rule, not fixed. Supersedes/absorbs the unfiled remainder of old nqtz (no longer in store — store reversion) which tracked the same split.
